newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-ANDERSSON REJOINS GOTHENBURG FOR EURO CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANDERSSON REJOINS GOTHENBURG FOR EURO CLASH.

text.p: Andreas Andersson will spearhead IFK Gothenburg's attack against Glasgow Rangers in their European Cup preliminary fixture on Wednesday -- despite having been sold to AC Milan in the off-season.

Andersson's transfer to the Italian side included a clause that allowed him to return to Gothenburg for this fixture and he is set to play despite having only two weeks of pre-season training under his belt.
IFK coach Mats Jingblad said he planned to play Andersson from the start but admitted to being "a little bit worried about his fitness".
"I'll have a chat with him before the start," he added.

Rangers manager Walter Smith said he did not think it was a good idea for Andersson to play for his old club. "He is a good player but it doesn't seem the ideal situation to me," he said. "I wonder what would happen if he got injured - I wouldn't want to put myself in that position."

Andersson's former Gothenburg team mates are well into their domestic season and are currently in their usual position at the top of the league. They warmed up for Wednesday's game with a 2-0 win over Vasteras.

Rangers, however, have had very little worthwhile activity. Bidding for a record 10th successive Scottish title, they won their opening league game 3-1 against Hearts and then put out a virtual reserve team to beat lowly Berwick 1-0 in the League Cup. Those games followed the 11-0 aggregate thrashing of GI Gotu of the Faroe Islands in the first preliminary round.

They travelled to Sweden on Tuesday without inspirational captain Brian Laudrup, who has chickenpox, but Paul Gascoigne, who has had only 45 minutes of competitive action so far this season, has been ruled fit to play after recovering from a calf strain.
Rangers' central defender Craig Moore and midfielder Ian Ferguson are suffering from an ankle injury and a hamstring strain respectively but are likely to play.
The winners of the two-legged tie advance to the expanded Champions' League while the losers go into the UEFA Cup.
